sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the power of Israel to draw down the revelation of Atzmus comes from the root of their souls being in the very Essence of the Blessed One, as illustrated by the analogy of a father and son.

translations.translation: And it can be said that the power that Israel has to draw down a revelation of this aspect,
is from the side of the root of their souls
[for the creation of man on the sixth day of Maaseh Bereishis
(Rosh Hashanah)
was when "And He blew into his nostrils the soul of life"34.
But not so the body of Adam HaRishon, which was formed from dust of the earth34
that had already been created
(as above)
on the first day35].
And the explanation of the matter is,
for it is written34
"And He blew into his nostrils the soul of life,"
and our master the Alter Rebbe explains36
as stated in the Zohar37
"One who blows, blows from within himself,"
and interprets it as from his innermost being and his pnimiyus,
meaning that
(the root)
of the soul is in His Essence, blessed be He.
And although it is drawn down there,
for just as a son is drawn from the brain of the father, so too, so to speak, the soul of every Jewish person is drawn from His thought and wisdom, blessed be He,
behold, this that the soul is in the aspect of His thought and wisdom, blessed be He, is like when it comes in a drawn-down manner,
but its root
(the true one)
is in His Essence, blessed be He.
For it is like in the analogy of a father and son,
that the root of the son is from the very essence of the father, above the aspect of revelations
(of the father),
therefore it is possible that the power of the son is greater than the power of the father38
because the root of the son is from the essential soul of the father, and in his essential soul the father is complete in all his powers39,
in this manner it is also with the souls of Israel,
"You are children to Hashem your G-d"40,
that their root is in His Essence, blessed be He
(which is above the aspect of revelations),
and therefore they have an advantage, so to speak, over the aspect of the revelations above,
in the manner of "the power of the son is greater than the power of the father."
And as our sages, of blessed memory, said41
"The Holy One, blessed be He, said, 'My children have defeated Me, My children have defeated Me,'"
"The Holy One, blessed be He" is Ein Sof as it comes in a drawn-down manner in the aspect of Kadosh and Baruch
[Kadosh is Sovev Kol Almin,
which is holy and separate from Hishtalshelus,
and Baruch is from the language of blessing and drawing down, like that which is drawn down to be Memale Kol Almin42],
and since the root of the souls is in His Essence, blessed be He
(which is above even the aspect of Kadosh),
therefore "The Holy One, blessed be He, said, 'My children have defeated Me, My children have defeated Me'"
[And this matter is particularly relevant to Rosh Hashanah,
as per the statement of our sages, of blessed memory43,

"When the ministering angels gather before the Holy One, blessed be He, to say 'When is Rosh Hashanah?' ... the Holy One, blessed be He, says to them, 'What are you asking Me? I and you will go to the Beis Din below.'"]
[This is the continuation of the previous statement.]
And particularly according to the teaching of the Maggid44
in explaining the statement of our sages, of blessed memory45
"Israel arose in thought,"
which is like the analogy of a son whose form is engraved in the thought of the father,
except that in human beings this applies specifically after the son is born,
but not so with the Blessed One,
even before Israel were created, their form was engraved in thought,
for with Him, blessed be He, the past and the future are one.
From this it is understood even more46,
that the root of the souls
("You are children to Hashem your G-d")
is in His Essence, blessed be He.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the soul's root is in a state of absolute concealment, requiring a "blowing with force" to draw it down, analogous to striking flint to produce fire.

translations.translation: And it can be said that this is what the Alter Rebbe said36
regarding "And He blew into his nostrils the soul of life,"
that it is in the aspect of a blowing with force, so to speak47,
for this need for a blowing with force is because the root of the soul is in the aspect of essential concealment,
a concealment that is not in existence,
and the drawing down from the aspect of a concealment that is not in existence is specifically through toil and effort.
For it is known that to draw down from a concealment that exists in reality, there is no need for toil and effort.
And like a flame that is attached to a coal,
for because even within the coal, fire exists in reality, only it is not seen and revealed externally
(a concealment that exists in reality),
therefore extracting the flame from the coal is without labor and effort.
But not so the drawing down from the aspect of a concealment that is not in existence, which is specifically through toil and effort.
And like extracting fire from flint,
for because the fire in the flint is in the aspect of a concealment that is not in existence,
therefore it is impossible to extract fire from it except through striking,
specifically with toil and effort.
And as all this is explained at length in the discourses of the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory48.
And this is what the Alter Rebbe said, that "And He blew into his nostrils the soul of life" is in the aspect of a blowing with force,
because the root of the souls is in the aspect of a concealment that is not in existence,
the aspect of Tzur
[And as explained in Likkutei Torah49
regarding the matter of Teshuvah, "And the spirit shall return to the G-d who gave it"50,
that the aspect of Elokim
("who gave it")
which is the root of the soul
(and from this perspective the soul is given in a manner of giving,
for anyone who
gives, gives with a generous eye52)
is the aspect of Tzur],
and therefore the drawing down from there is through a blowing with force.
And because the root of the souls of Israel is in His Essence, blessed be He, therefore they have the ability to draw down into the world a revelation of the Essence of Ein Sof.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the revelation of Atzmus in the world is achieved by first drawing it down into one's own body, which is the aspect of "Koh," through the principle of "measure for measure."

translations.translation: And behold, the above is an explanation of this, that it is within the power of Israel to draw down a revelation of the Essence of Ein Sof.
However, that they draw down this revelation into the world,
the connection of this aspect with the aspect of Koh33,
it can be said that it is by means of their drawing down the revelation of their soul into their body.
For the body of man
(which was formed from dust of the earth that was created on the 25th of Elul)
is the aspect of Koh,
and by his effecting a revelation of G-dliness in his body,
through this he draws down a revelation of G-dliness also into the world.
For "with the measure that a person measures, they measure for him"53,
and therefore, by a person drawing down the revelation of the aspect of Zeh into the aspect of Koh that is in himself,
through this the revelation of the aspect of Zeh is drawn down also into the aspect of Koh of the entire world54.
And like Adam HaRishon, who said to all of creation, "Come, let us prostrate ourselves and bow, let us kneel before Hashem our Maker"55,
for this that he effected bittul in all of creation
(that is outside of him)
was through his own action of bittul.
And as per the interpretation of "let us prostrate ourselves"
(and not "they prostrated themselves"),
meaning56
that
(also)
he himself would prostrate himself and be in a state of bittul.
And the explanation of the matter
(this that the drawing down of the revelation of G-dliness into the world is through the prior drawing down into the body of man),
behold, the name Adam is from the term "Adameh l'Elyon" (I will be like the Most High)57,
and it can be said that this applies to the soul of man and also to the body of man,
as it is written58
"Let us make man ... in our likeness"59.
And just as the body of Adam HaRishon was the handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He60,
so too is it regarding the body of every single Jew,
for "you are called Adam" after Adam HaRishon
(as above).
And this that every single Jew is called Adam from the term "Adameh l'Elyon,"
both from the aspect of his soul and from the aspect of his body,
is an eternal matter in which change does not apply.
And as it is written61
"And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation,"
and it can be said that "a kingdom of priests" refers to the soul and "a holy nation" refers to the body62,
and regarding both it is said "And you shall be to Me,"
for every place where "to Me" is stated, it never ceases63.
And therefore, through the service of man to draw down a revelation of G-dliness into his body,
through this a revelation of G-dliness is drawn down also into the world.
